**Describe the bug**
When loading additional items from a paginated response using the "List More Prompts" or "List More Tools" buttons all previously loaded prompts or tools are discarded and only the newly loaded items are shown in the pane.

The "List More Resources" and "List More Templates" buttons add additional items to the existing list as expected.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Run inspector
2. Connect to a server that returns paginated tools or prompts in response
3. Click List Prompts (or List Tools) button
4. List More Prompts or (List More Prompts) button

**Expected behavior**
Additional prompts are added to list of previously loaded prompts.

**Actual behavior**
Newly fetched prompts replace previously loaded prompts.

**Additional context**
This is happening because the `listTools` and `listPrompts` functions set the state to the newly fetched items instead of concatenating them with the items in the existing state, as `listResources` does.

title: Path resolution library doesn't handle MacOS commands correctly
body: This [spawn-rx issue](https://github.com/anaisbetts/spawn-rx/issues/19) is affecting use of `@modelcontextprotocol/inspector` on MacOS. `findActualExecutable` returns the wrong value on MacOS if the user's Node version management uses symlinks. In my case, `spawn-rx` is causing `bun` to resolve to `[redacted-path]/.volta/bin/volta-shim` when it should resolve to `[redacted-path]/.volta/bin/bun`. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. title: Dynamic client registration should be optional
body:
Currently getting this error if the target MCP server uses auth but does not provide dynamic client registration capabilities:

![Screenshot of an error message in the DevTools](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c36c0946-f8cb-41ec-9bea-a7945db69dd5)

[Per spec](https://spec.modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/basic/authorization/):

>MCP clients and servers SHOULD support the [OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration Protocol](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591) to allow MCP clients to obtain OAuth client IDs without user interaction. This provides a standardized way for clients to automatically register with new servers, which is crucial for MCP because:
>
>- Clients cannot know all possible servers in advance
>- Manual registration would create friction for users
>- It enables seamless connection to new servers
>- Servers can implement their own registration policies
>
>Any MCP servers that do not support Dynamic Client Registration need to provide alternative ways to obtain a client ID (and, if applicable, client secret). For one of these servers, MCP clients will have to either:
>1. Hardcode a client ID (and, if applicable, client secret) specifically for that MCP server, or
>1. Present a UI to users that allows them to enter these details, after registering an OAuth client themselves (e.g., through a configuration interface hosted by the server).

There probably should be some graceful degradation here, or:

1. Assuming that the server will handle client assignment (e.g., in public client cases), -OR-
2. Provide some avenue to request a client ID.

title: Bug: MCP Inspector Fails to Send Input Data When Switching Tools Without Changing Values
body:
#### **Describe the bug**
In the MCP Inspector app (version 0.6.0), there is a bug when switching between tools defined using Server-Sent Events (SSE). I have defined two tools: "add" and "multiply." When running one tool (e.g., "add") repeatedly with the same input values, it works consistently. However, when switching to the other tool (e.g., "multiply") without changing the input values—which are retained by default from the previous tool—the inspector client fails to send the input data to the server. This results in a server-side error stating that the fields "a" and "b" are required. The issue only resolves after manually changing the input values, at which point the client correctly sends the data to the server.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c242d29-1fb8-49bf-852c-01278df9b82a)

#### **To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Open the MCP Inspector app (version 0.6.0).
2. Connect to the server via SSE (e.g., Transport Type: SSE, URL: `http://localhost:3333/sse`).
3. In the "Tools" section, select the "add" tool (designed to add two numbers).
4. Enter values in the input fields (e.g., `a = 10`, `b = 5`).
5. Click "Run Tool" multiple times to confirm the "add" tool works consistently.
6. Switch to the "multiply" tool (designed to multiply two numbers), keeping the same input values (`a = 10`, `b = 5`) as they are retained by default.
7. Click "Run Tool" for the "multiply" tool.
8. Observe the server error indicating that the fields "a" and "b" are required.
9. Change one of the input values (e.g., `a = 10` to `a = 15`).
10. Click "Run Tool" again and observe that the "multiply" tool now executes successfully.

#### **Expected behavior**
When switching between tools (e.g., from "add" to "multiply") with the same input values retained by default, the inspector client should still send the input data (`a` and `b`) to the server. The tool should execute successfully without requiring manual changes to the input fields, and the server should not return a "field required" error since the fields are already populated with valid values.

#### **Logs**
When attempting to run the "multiply" tool without changing the input values after switching from "add," the server returns the following error:

```
Error executing tool multiply: 2 validation errors for multiplyArguments
a
  Field required [type=missing, input_value={}, input_type=dict]
    For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.10/v/missing
b
  Field required [type=missing, input_value={}, input_type=dict]
    For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.10/v/missing
```

#### **Additional context**
- This issue occurs in MCP Inspector version 0.6.0.
- The tools "add" and "multiply" are defined using Server-Sent Events (SSE) and connected to the server at `http://localhost:3333/sse`.
- The "add" tool takes two arguments ("a" and "b") and returns their sum. The "multiply" tool takes the same arguments and returns their product.
- The input fields "a" and "b" are pre-filled with the values from the previous tool when switching between tools.
- The bug does not occur when running the same tool repeatedly with unchanged inputs; it only occurs when switching tools without modifying the input values.
- Manually changing the input values (even slightly) after switching tools triggers the client to send the data to the server, resolving the issue.

title: Usability issue for long-running tasks
body:
The MCP Inspector client's request timeout mechanism does not reset when a `notifications/progress` message is received for an ongoing request. This deviates from a suggested behavior in the MCP specification, potentially causing premature timeouts for long-running operations that provide progress updates.

**Specification Reference:**

The MCP specification document `basic/lifecycle.md` under the "Timeouts" section states:

> Implementations **MAY** choose to reset the timeout clock when receiving a [progress notification] corresponding to the request, as this implies that work is actually happening. However, implementations **SHOULD** always enforce a maximum timeout, regardless of progress notifications, to limit the impact of a misbehaving client or server.

**Current Behavior:**

In `client/src/lib/hooks/useConnection.ts`, the `makeRequest` function initiates a `setTimeout` when a request is sent. This timeout is only cleared when the request promise resolves or rejects (within the `finally` block). Receiving a `notifications/progress` (handled separately via `setNotificationHandler`) does not interact with or reset this timeout timer.

**Expected Behavior:**

Following the suggestion in the specification, the client *could* reset the request timeout timer each time a relevant `notifications/progress` is received. This would allow long-running operations that provide regular progress updates to continue without timing out prematurely, as long as progress is being reported within the timeout window. A maximum overall timeout should still be considered.

title: Incorrect URL in sse.js when providing a custom path
body:
**Summary**
When adding an sse server using a custom path (e.g. `http://localhost:3001/custom/path/sse`), the server sends messages requests to `http://localhost:3001` instead of `http://localhost:3001/custom/path`.

**Steps to reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Launch an SSE MCP server on a custom path (e.g. `http://localhost:3001/custom/path`)
2. Connect the inspector to it using the UI (enter `http://localhost:3001/custom/path/sse` in the URL field)
3. Try to connect. Instead of successful connection, yo get an error because it sends requests to `http://localhost:3001`

**Issue**
`this._endpoint = new URL(messageEvent.data, this._url);` in `sse.js `ignores custom path, which is needed for the upcoming requests.

**Impact**
 No connection is possible

title: [Feature Request] Add Request/Response log Panel for Better Debugging
body:
### Summary
I would like to suggest adding a **Request/Response Dump Panel** in the MCP Inspector tool to improve the developer experience during tool testing and debugging.

### Motivation
Currently, when testing a Tool through the MCP Inspector, we can see the final output result, but we do not have visibility over:
- The exact **JSON body** that was posted.
- The **headers** sent (such as `Content-Type` and `Accept`).
- The full **response body**, including potential errors.
- The **HTTP status codes** returned by the MCP server.

This lack of visibility makes it harder to debug issues like:
- Incorrect input JSON structures.
- Deserialization or binding problems.
- Contract schema mismatches.
- Unexpected server-side behavior.

Adding a Request/Response Dump would make it much easier to understand and debug what is happening internally, especially when working with complex Tool schemas or diagnosing integration issues.

### Proposed Solution
- After the user submits a Tool call:
  - Capture and display the **HTTP Request** details:
    - URL
    - Headers
    - Request Body (JSON)
  - Capture and display the **HTTP Response** details:
    - Status Code
    - Headers
    - Response Body (JSON or error message)

- Add a **"Debug Mode"** flag (e.g., a simple toggle button) in the UI that, when enabled, shows a collapsible panel or a new tab with:
  - **[Request]** section
  - **[Response]** section

title: OAuth with streamable HTTP does not work
body:
**Describe the bug**
When trying to initialize a connection using streamable HTTP, if OAuth is supported then the inspector should get a `401` and initiate the OAuth flow.

Right now, the proxy is "swallowing" this `401` error and it never gets to the client to actually initialize the OAuth flow.

**To Reproduce**

Try to connect to a server that supports OAuth with streamable HTTP.

First, the client (browser) will attempt to make a `POST` to:

```
http://localhost:6277/mcp?url={server_url}&transportType=streamable-http
```

The MCP server properly responds with a `401` (as per [the specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/authorization#2-2-example%3A-authorization-code-grant)).

However, this `401` is swallowed by the proxy which prints out:

```sh
Connected to Streamable HTTP transport
Connected MCP client to backing server transport
Created streamable web app transport 7c2996a2-b5e6-4b69-86e1-0885892edf49
Error from MCP server: Error: Error POSTing to endpoint (HTTP 401): {"error":"Missing or invalid authorization header"}
    at StreamableHTTPClientTransport.send (file://[redacted-path]/Library/pnpm/store/v3/tmp/dlx-10003/node_modules/.pnpm/@modelcontextprotocol+sdk@1.11.1/node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/client/streamableHttp.js:263:23)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:95:5)
Error from MCP server: Error: Error POSTing to endpoint (HTTP 401): {"error":"Missing or invalid authorization header"}
    at StreamableHTTPClientTransport.send (file://[redacted-path]/Library/pnpm/store/v3/tmp/dlx-10003/node_modules/.pnpm/@modelcontextprotocol+sdk@1.11.1/node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/client/streamableHttp.js:263:23)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:95:5)
```

Here, `{"error":"Missing or invalid authorization header"}` is the error returned by our server when we expect OAuth to be initiated by the MCP client.

When this happens, the `POST` to the `/mcp` proxy hangs until it times out. The `401` never makes it to the client.

Note that the flow with SSE and OAuth works just fine. This seems to be an issue somewhere in the proxy itself.

**Expected behavior**

When the MCP server returns a `401`, initiate OAuth on the MCP client to get a token to use to authenticate with the server.

title: Local Proxy Causes Session ID Mismatch with Streamable HTTP Servers
body:
## tl;dr
MCP Inspector v0.14.0's local proxy (127.0.0.1:6277) is creating its own session ID for Streamable HTTP connections to remote MCP servers, instead of using the authoritative Mcp-Session-Id provided by the server in its initial response. This causes subsequent requests to be rejected by the MCP server due to an unrecognized session ID, leading to "Connection Error" in the Inspector UI. This issue prevents proper testing and debugging of cloud-deployed MCP servers. The local proxy needs to transparently pass through the server-generated Mcp-Session-Id header.

## Issue Summary

MCP Inspector v0.14.0 fails to connect to MCP servers using Streamable HTTP transport due to a session ID mismatch between the local proxy server and the remote MCP server. The root cause is that the Inspector's local proxy (running at `127.0.0.1:6277`) generates its own session ID instead of using the authoritative session ID provided by the MCP server in the `Mcp-Session-Id` response header.

## Environment

- **MCP Inspector Version**: v0.14.0
- **Transport Type**: Streamable HTTP
- **MCP Server**: Fully compliant with MCP Streamable HTTP specification (2025-03-26)
- **Server URL**: `https://[masked-server-url]/mcp`
- **Local Proxy**: `127.0.0.1:6277` (detected from logs)

## Expected Behavior (Per MCP Specification)

According to the MCP Streamable HTTP specification, the correct session management flow should be:

1. **Client sends initialize request**:
   ```http
   POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
   Content-Type: application/json
   Accept: application/json, text/event-stream
   Authorization: Bearer <token>
   
   {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{...}}
   ```

2. **Server generates session ID and responds**:
   ```http
   HTTP/1.1 200 OK
   Mcp-Session-Id: <server-generated-session-id>
   Content-Type: application/json
   
   {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{...}}
   ```

3. **Client uses server-provided session ID for all subsequent requests**:
   ```http
   POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
   Mcp-Session-Id: <server-generated-session-id>
   Content-Type: application/json
   
   {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}
   ```

## Actual Behavior (Problematic)

The current MCP Inspector implementation appears to follow this problematic flow:

1. **Inspector's local proxy generates its own session ID** (e.g., `72e026fd-...`)
2. **MCP server generates its own session ID** (e.g., `28d52579-...`) and returns it in `Mcp-Session-Id` header
3. **Inspector continues using proxy-generated session ID instead of server-provided one**
4. **Server rejects subsequent requests** due to unrecognized session ID
5. **Inspector shows "Connection Error, is your MCP server running?"**

## Evidence from Server Logs

Our MCP server logs clearly show the session ID mismatch:

```
2025-06-05 13:37:50,370 - streamable_http_transport - INFO - Streamable HTTP transport initialized with endpoint: /mcp
2025-06-05 13:38:06,457 - cloud_mcp_server - INFO - MCP Streamable HTTP request: POST /mcp
2025-06-05 13:38:06,459 - streamable_http_transport - INFO - Created new session: cX-y@8"+j3uGKYOK:Uc$wYx+>N1(R&
2025-06-05 13:38:06,459 - streamable_http_transport - INFO - Processing message for session cX-y@8"+j3uGKYOK:Uc$wYx+>N1(R& : initialize
INFO: 169.254.169.126:65120 - "POST /mcp HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
```

The server successfully:
- ✅ Receives initialize request
- ✅ Generates cryptographically secure session ID: `cX-y@8"+j3uGKYOK:Uc$wYx+>N1(R&`
- ✅ Returns 200 OK with `Mcp-Session-Id` header
- ❌ But Inspector never uses this session ID for subsequent requests

## Server Implementation (Specification Compliant)

Our server implementation correctly follows the MCP specification:

```python
async def _handle_initialize_request(self, request: Request, body: Dict[str, Any]) -> JSONResponse:
    # Extract authentication info if available
    auth_info = {}
    if "Authorization" in request.headers:
        auth_info["authorization"] = request.headers["Authorization"]
    
    # Create new session (server is authority for session IDs)
    session_id = self.session_manager.create_session(auth_info)
    
    # Process initialize message
    result = await self._process_message(body, session_id)
    
    # Return result with session ID in header (per specification)
    return JSONResponse(
        content=result,
        headers={"Mcp-Session-Id": session_id}  # ← SPECIFICATION COMPLIANT
    )
```

Session ID generation uses cryptographically secure methods with visible ASCII characters only (0x21-0x7E range), as required by the specification.

## Root Cause Analysis

The issue lies in the **MCP Inspector's local proxy server behavior**:

### Current (Incorrect) Proxy Behavior:
1. Proxy generates its own session ID
2. Proxy sends this ID to Inspector UI
3. Proxy may ignore or replace the `Mcp-Session-Id` header from the real MCP server
4. Inspector uses proxy-generated ID for subsequent requests
5. Real MCP server rejects requests with unknown session ID

### Required (Correct) Proxy Behavior:
1. Proxy transparently forwards initialize request to MCP server
2. MCP server generates authoritative session ID
3. **Proxy must pass through the `Mcp-Session-Id` header from server response**
4. Inspector UI uses server-provided session ID for all subsequent communication
5. Proxy transparently forwards all requests with correct session ID

## Reproduction Steps

1. Configure MCP Inspector v0.14.0 with Streamable HTTP transport
2. Use any compliant MCP server (we've tested with our GCP-deployed server)
3. Attempt to connect
4. Observe "Connection Error" in Inspector UI
5. Check server logs to confirm session ID mismatch

## Configuration Used for Testing

```json
{
  "name": "Remote MCP Server (Streamable HTTP)",
  "transportType": "http",
  "url": "https://[masked-server-url]/mcp",
  "headers": {
    "Authorization": "Bearer test-api-key-12345"
  }
}
```

## Workaround

Direct HTTP requests work perfectly, confirming our server implementation is correct:

```bash
# This works - direct connection bypassing Inspector proxy
curl -X POST https://[masked-server-url]/mcp \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer test-api-key-12345" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-03-26"}}'
```

Returns:
```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Mcp-Session-Id: <server-generated-session-id>
Content-Type: application/json

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{...}}
```

## Requested Fix

Please update the MCP Inspector's local proxy server (running at `127.0.0.1:6277`) to:

1. **Stop generating its own session IDs** for remote MCP servers
2. **Transparently pass through `Mcp-Session-Id` headers** from server responses
3. **Ensure the Inspector UI uses server-provided session IDs** for all subsequent requests
4. **Maintain proxy-generated session IDs only for local/STDIO transports** where the proxy acts as the actual MCP server

## Additional Context

This issue affects any organization deploying MCP servers in cloud environments using Streamable HTTP transport. It prevents proper testing and debugging of remote MCP implementations, which is a critical use case for MCP Inspector.

Our implementation has been tested and verified to be fully compliant with the MCP Streamable HTTP specification (protocol version 2025-03-26), including:
- ✅ JSON-RPC 2.0 compliance
- ✅ Proper Accept header validation
- ✅ DNS rebinding protection
- ✅ Cryptographically secure session ID generation
- ✅ 202 Accepted responses for notifications
- ✅ Single message processing (no batch support)

## Server Implementation Repository

Our fully compliant MCP Streamable HTTP server implementation is available for reference and testing. The issue is definitively in the Inspector's proxy behavior, not in compliant server implementations.

---

**Impact**: High - Blocks testing and development of cloud-deployed MCP servers  
**Priority**: High - Core functionality for remote MCP debugging and development  
**Scope**: MCP Inspector local proxy server session management
label: RESOLVED_COMPLETED

Describe the bug

When using MCP Inspector, if a request is made with a syntactically invalid JSON string as a parameter, the Inspector does not send the invalid data. Instead, it silently re-sends the valid parameters from the last successful request. This makes debugging tools extremely difficult, as the server receives stale, unexpected data, and there is no error shown on the client-side UI to indicate the actual input was ignored.

Start MCP Inspector pointing to a tool server.
Bash

npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@latest

Select a tool that accepts a JSON object as a parameter (e.g., a filters parameter).
First Request (Valid): Execute the tool with a valid JSON string.
Example input: {"status": "active"}

Observe the server logs to confirm it correctly received the parameters: {'status': 'active'}.
Second Request (Invalid): In the same parameter field, enter a malformed JSON string.
Example input: {"status": "inactive",} (note the trailing comma).
Execute the tool again and check the server logs.


Expected behavior

On the second request, the tool server should receive the malformed string or a null value for the filters parameter. This should ideally trigger a server-side validation error (like an HTTP 400 Bad Request), correctly indicating that the client sent invalid data. The server should not receive the data from the first request.

title: Metadata discovery - handling `openid-configuration` not just `oauth-authorization-server`
body:
**Describe the bug**
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) Inspector, when performing Authorization Server (AS) metadata discovery via the authorization_servers field in Protected Resource Metadata (PRM) (RFC 9728), currently only attempts to fetch metadata from the `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` endpoint. Many common Authorization Servers, including Azure Active Directory, primarily expose their metadata via the `/.well-known/openid-configuration` endpoint, as defined by OpenID Connect Discovery. This prevents the inspector from successfully discovering AS metadata for such providers, leading to incomplete authorization flow setup.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Set up a Protected Resource (your resource server) to expose its metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (RFC 9728).
2. In this Protected Resource Metadata, include an `authorization_servers` entry where the issuer identifier points to an OpenID Connect-compliant Authorization Server that uses `/.well-known/openid-configuration` (e.g., an Azure AD tenant issuer URL like `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant-id}/v2.0`).
3. Use the modelcontextprotocol/inspector to analyze this Protected Resource by Guided Auth flow / Metadata discovery
4. Observe the inspector's attempt to discover the Authorization Server metadata.

**Expected behavior**
The modelcontextprotocol/inspector should successfully discover the Authorization Server metadata by attempting to fetch from both `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and `/.well-known/openid-configuration` when processing an issuer identifier from the authorization_servers array in Protected Resource Metadata. Upon successful discovery, it should report the AS's capabilities and endpoints.


**Additional context**
The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata (RFC 8414) and OpenID Connect Discovery (OpenID.Discovery) specifications both define mechanisms for Authorization Server metadata publication. OpenID Connect Discovery is effectively an extension of the OAuth 2.0 metadata, and many identity providers opt to expose a single metadata document at the `/.well-known/openid-configuration` endpoint that satisfies both specifications. To ensure full compatibility and successful discovery across a wide range of OAuth/OIDC providers, the modelcontextprotocol/inspector should explicitly check for `/.well-known/openid-configuration` as a valid discovery endpoint for authorization server metadata.

title: 📌 Feature Request: Ability to Configure audience in OAuth Requests
body:
Summary
Add support for configuring the audience (aud) parameter in OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect flows initiated via MCP Inspector.

Motivation
Currently, MCP Inspector does not allow setting a custom audience parameter when requesting access tokens. As a result:
	•	Tokens are issued for the default Auth0 Management API (aud = https://<tenant>.auth0.com/api/v2/)
	•	This often leads to unexpected scopes or encrypted tokens (JWE) depending on API settings
	•	Users intending to test custom APIs with their own audience identifiers cannot do so via MCP Inspector
	•	The token’s behavior (payload, encryption, scopes) becomes incorrect for anything other than the Management API

Proposed Solution
Allow users to configure a custom audience value as part of:
	•	The OAuth authorize request
	•	The /oauth/token request (especially for client credentials flow)

This could be exposed as a simple input field in the UI when setting up an OAuth test session, or as part of an advanced configuration section.

Benefits
	•	Supports testing real-world OAuth setups involving custom APIs
	•	Aligns with Auth0, Azure AD, Okta, and other providers that require an explicit audience
	•	Avoids the accidental issuance of encrypted or mis-scoped tokens
	•	Matches behavior already supported in tools like Postman and curl

References
	•	[Auth0: How to pass audience](https://auth0.com/docs/get-started/authentication-and-authorization-flow/call-your-api-using-the-authorization-code-flow)
	•	[OpenID Connect Spec - Audience Claim](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#IDToken)
